Authority notice

Documenting a route never authorizes it. The charter and code win over a conflicting sheet. No direct provider-to-provider channel exists; route every exchange through the Director.

alias_note
Firecrawl is a LangGraph-primary-only public search lane. It shares Perplexity's fail-closed public research contract and public-search transport class but is its own lane with its own allocation; it is not a Perplexity alias.

Team and allocation

team
lane_only
lane_class
public_search_transport
summary
Public search transport on the LangGraph primary path only, under the same fail-closed public research contract as Perplexity. It has an allocation in the mixed, public research, and enterprise profiles but no charter role, committee seat, or legacy adapter, and a nonzero target is not evidence that the route is operational.

Platform limitations

  • limitation
    No Firecrawl variable appears in .env.example or docs/provider-setup.html; the lane's credential names exist only in the primary transport authentication map.
    source
    src/director_orchestrator/primary_transports.py:_PROVIDER_AUTH_ENVIRONMENT
  • limitation
    The legacy provider registry has no Firecrawl adapter; the lane can execute only on the LangGraph primary path through the public-search transport.
    source
    docs/provider-allocation-profiles.html
  • limitation
    Firecrawl is not a supported Windows host-bridge lane and has no browser provider-UI eligibility.
    source
    src/director_orchestrator/host_provider_bridge.py:SUPPORTED_HOST_LANES; docs/team-operating-charter.html
  • limitation
    The public-search transport rejects every external effect.
    source
    src/director_orchestrator/primary_default.py:_PRIMARY_PUBLIC_RESEARCH_LANES

direct_provider_to_provider_channels_exist

notes
  • Firecrawl evidence reaches any other lane only as a Director-declared dependency outcome after a primary-team member evaluates it.
  • Firecrawl never posts to the Slack thread and never receives another provider's output.
